summary_responses.response: The Department of Justice’s Office of Justice Programs has proposed a new Privacy Act system of records, “Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS) Statistical Data,” designated JUSTICE/OJP-017. The system will store information gathered through questionnaires, surveys, interviews, focus groups, and administrative records to support BJS’s mission to collect, analyze, publish, and disseminate statistics on crime, offenders, victims, and justice systems at all levels of government. It covers survey respondents and people appearing in criminal or civil justice records, and may contain direct identifiers as well as criminal-history, victimization, demographic, employment, medical, and other sensitive information. BJS and its data-collection agents may use the information only for statistical and research purposes, must apply strict privacy and confidentiality protections, and may not use individual-level data for enforcement, regulatory action, or decisions about personal benefits. The notice takes effect upon publication, with comments on its routine uses due by November 16, 2026, and DOJ has reported the new system to OMB and Congress.

The rule updates definitions and auction terminology, removes outdated references, and clarifies that certain calculations for inflation-protected securities remain unchanged. Simulations and a live Kubernetes deployment, where DiffTry operates as a drop-in service-mesh plugin without application changes, closely match the analysis and demonstrate effective network-wide prioritization.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) issued a direct final rule updating its title 5 Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to codify statutory amendments enacted in January 2021 and December 2023, along with related policy guidance. The rule counts virtually all Federal civilian service—including temporary and intermittent service—toward the 12-month FMLA eligibility requirement, although employees must still hold a covered position to use title 5 FMLA leave. It also allows honorable active service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps to count toward that requirement, in any combination with qualifying civilian service, and these changes also affect eligibility for paid parental leave. Additionally, the rule reflects that annual or sick leave provided under an authority outside title 5 may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave and excludes Veterans Health Administration employees covered by a separate leave system under 38 U.S.C. 7421 from title 5 FMLA coverage. The rule is effective December 14, 2026, unless OPM receives significant adverse comments by November 16, 2026, in which case it will withdraw the affected provisions and issue a proposed rule.
